metadata.title: Advancing language education with ChatGPT: A path to cultivate 21st-century digital skills

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used a classroom-based sample of high-school English learners in three schools in Iran and administered a researcher-developed questionnaire after integrating ChatGPT into English instruction. The manuscript does not report the use of complex survey sampling weights or any student/school-level design weights, and it does not provide any weight variable names (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) or replicate-weight procedures (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because the analysis is based on PLS-SEM of self-report Likert-scale constructs rather than ILSA-style achievement PVs, there is no plausible international weight variable to apply. Therefore, weighting is treated as not used/undocumented, and results should be interpreted as within-sample relationships rather than population-representative estimates.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This paper does not use ILSA-style cognitive achievement outcomes with Plausible Values; instead, it models latent constructs measured via self-report Likert-scale questionnaire items (e.g., information management, information evaluation). Because the dependent variables are not PV-based achievement scores, PV handling is not applicable. The manuscript also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure (e.g., listwise deletion, imputation), which is a reporting gap for questionnaire-based SEM/PLS-SEM analyses where item nonresponse can occur.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The study recruited all students participating in the second author’s English classes in three schools during the second semester of the 2023–2024 academic year in Iran. Participants were high-school students expected to pass the national Vision 3 course (third year of high school) and were integrated into a ChatGPT-assisted instructional procedure. The manuscript reports the total number of participants (236) and demographic breakdowns, but it does not specify additional inclusion/exclusion rules beyond participation and consent, nor does it report any analytic-sample exclusions for missing questionnaire items.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning study (Iran, 2023–2024 high school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R-square (INFOM)=0.092; Q2=0.044; SRMR=0.06. Path coefficients (bootstrap): PER→INFOM β=0.091 (t=0.940, p=0.347) not significant; ANT→INFOM β=0.097 (t=1.445, p=0.146) not significant; DSA→INFOM β=-0.107 (t=1.419, p=0.156) not significant; INT→INFOM β=0.016 (t=0.210, p=0.834) not significant; ACC→INFOM β=0.212 (t=3.444, p=0.001) accepted.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning study the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, ChatGPT anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, ChatGPT interactivity, and ChatGPT accuracy & responsiveness to predict information management, finding that only ChatGPT accuracy & responsiveness had a significant positive effect (ACC→INFOM β=0.212, p=0.001) while the other ChatGPT features were not significant. This indicates that emphasizing reliable and timely ChatGPT responses may be more effective for helping learners organize and manage information than focusing on personalization, anthropomorphic cues, or interactivity alone.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning study (Iran, 2023–2024 high school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R-square (INFOE)=0.230; Q2=0.134; SRMR=0.06. Path coefficients (bootstrap): PER→INFOE β=0.334 (t=4.864, p=0.000) accepted; ANT→INFOE β=0.041 (t=0.721, p=0.471) not significant; DSA→INFOE β=0.003 (t=0.047, p=0.969) not significant; INT→INFOE β=0.174 (t=2.846, p=0.004) accepted; ACC→INFOE β=0.142 (t=2.156, p=0.031) accepted.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning study the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, ChatGPT anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, ChatGPT interactivity, and ChatGPT accuracy & responsiveness to predict information evaluation, finding that personalization, interactivity, and accuracy & responsiveness had significant positive effects (PER→INFOE β=0.334, p=0.000; INT→INFOE β=0.174, p=0.004; ACC→INFOE β=0.142, p=0.031) while anthropomorphism and digital self-authenticity were not significant. This indicates that instructional designs that give learners meaningful choice, interactive dialogue, and trustworthy responses can strengthen learners’ ability to judge the usefulness and reliability of AI-provided information.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning study (Iran, 2023–2024 high school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R-square (DCM)=0.076; Q2=0.037; SRMR=0.06. Path coefficients (bootstrap): PER→DCM β=-0.017 (t=0.222, p=0.824) not significant; ANT→DCM β=0.023 (t=0.360, p=0.719) not significant; DSA→DCM β=0.003 (t=0.042, p=0.967) not significant; INT→DCM β=0.149 (t=1.986, p=0.047) accepted; ACC→DCM β=0.183 (t=2.868, p=0.004) accepted.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning study the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, ChatGPT anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, ChatGPT interactivity, and ChatGPT accuracy & responsiveness to predict digital communication skills, finding that only interactivity and accuracy & responsiveness were significant positive predictors (INT→DCM β=0.149, p=0.047; ACC→DCM β=0.183, p=0.004) while personalization, anthropomorphism, and digital self-authenticity were not significant. This indicates that to improve learners’ ability to transmit AI-generated information appropriately, teachers should prioritize interactive use of ChatGPT and ensure learners receive accurate, timely outputs.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning study (Iran, 2023–2024 high school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R-square (COL)=0.118; Q2=0.083; SRMR=0.06. Path coefficients (bootstrap): PER→COL β=0.185 (t=2.806, p=0.005) accepted; ANT→COL β=-0.237 (t=4.042, p=0.000) not significant (rejected); DSA→COL β=-0.120 (t=2.066, p=0.039) not significant (rejected); INT→COL β=-0.019 (t=0.262, p=0.793) not significant; ACC→COL β=0.143 (t=2.091, p=0.037) accepted.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning study the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, ChatGPT anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, ChatGPT interactivity, and ChatGPT accuracy & responsiveness to predict collaborative digital skills, finding that personalization and accuracy & responsiveness had significant positive effects (PER→COL β=0.185, p=0.005; ACC→COL β=0.143, p=0.037) while anthropomorphism and digital self-authenticity showed negative paths and were not supported as significant positive effects. This indicates that collaborative skill development may require carefully designed personalization and reliable outputs, while anthropomorphic features may risk reducing learners’ willingness to collaborate with peers.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning study (Iran, 2023–2024 high school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R-square (CRT)=0.304; Q2=0.218; SRMR=0.06. Path coefficients (bootstrap): PER→CRT β=0.232 (t=3.850, p=0.000) accepted; ANT→CRT β=0.043 (t=0.748, p=0.455) not significant; DSA→CRT β=0.159 (t=2.363, p=0.018) accepted; INT→CRT β=0.447 (t=6.711, p=0.000) accepted; ACC→CRT β=-0.062 (t=0.922, p=0.357) not significant.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning study the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, ChatGPT anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, ChatGPT interactivity, and ChatGPT accuracy & responsiveness to predict critical-thinking digital skills, finding that personalization, digital self-authenticity, and interactivity were significant positive predictors (PER→CRT β=0.232, p=0.000; DSA→CRT β=0.159, p=0.018; INT→CRT β=0.447, p=0.000) while accuracy & responsiveness and anthropomorphism were not significant. This indicates that fostering interactive dialogue and learners’ perceived authenticity with AI may be more important than response speed/accuracy alone for strengthening critical evaluation behaviors.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning study (Iran, 2023–2024 high school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R-square (CRE)=0.237; Q2=0.144; SRMR=0.06. Path coefficients (bootstrap): PER→CRE β=0.218 (t=3.280, p=0.001) accepted; ANT→CRE β=0.078 (t=1.317, p=0.188) not significant; DSA→CRE β=0.171 (t=2.351, p=0.019) accepted; INT→CRE β=0.249 (t=3.996, p=0.000) accepted; ACC→CRE β=0.147 (t=2.198, p=0.028) accepted.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning study the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, ChatGPT anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, ChatGPT interactivity, and ChatGPT accuracy & responsiveness to predict creative digital skills, finding that personalization, digital self-authenticity, interactivity, and accuracy & responsiveness all had significant positive effects (PER→CRE β=0.218, p=0.001; DSA→CRE β=0.171, p=0.019; INT→CRE β=0.249, p=0.000; ACC→CRE β=0.147, p=0.028) while anthropomorphism was not significant. This indicates that creative digital skill development benefits from multiple functional supports—choice, interactive engagement, trustworthy responses, and perceived authenticity—rather than from anthropomorphic presentation alone.

main_findings.dataset_used: ChatGPT-assisted language learning study (Iran, 2023–2024 high school English classes)
main_findings.performance_metrics: PLS-SEM structural model: R-square (PS)=0.359; Q2=0.219; SRMR=0.06. Path coefficients (bootstrap): PER→PS β=0.052 (t=0.940, p=0.347) not significant; ANT→PS β=0.179 (t=2.628, p=0.009) accepted; DSA→PS β=0.083 (t=1.401, p=0.161) not significant; INT→PS β=0.379 (t=6.327, p=0.000) accepted; ACC→PS β=0.254 (t=3.887, p=0.000) accepted.
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ChatGPT-assisted language learning study the study leveraged ChatGPT personalization, ChatGPT anthropomorphism, digital self-authenticity, ChatGPT interactivity, and ChatGPT accuracy & responsiveness to predict problem-solving digital skills, finding that anthropomorphism, interactivity, and accuracy & responsiveness were significant positive predictors (ANT→PS β=0.179, p=0.009; INT→PS β=0.379, p=0.000; ACC→PS β=0.254, p=0.000) while personalization and digital self-authenticity were not significant. This indicates that to improve learners’ ability to use AI for solving problems, teachers should design tasks that encourage interactive use, provide accurate responses, and can leverage anthropomorphic cues to support engagement with problem-solving.

data.outcome_summary: This study integrates ChatGPT into high-school English instruction in three Iranian schools (2023–2024) and uses PLS-SEM to model seven latent 21st-century digital-skill constructs measured via a 1–5 Likert questionnaire. With N=236 learners, the structural model shows meaningful explained variance for several outcomes (e.g., R²=0.359 for problem-solving, 0.304 for critical thinking, 0.237 for creativity, and 0.230 for information evaluation), with SRMR=0.06 and acceptable measurement validity (Cronbach’s alpha/composite reliability and HTMT <0.85). The strongest paths are from ChatGPT interactivity to critical thinking (β=0.447, p=0.000) and to problem-solving (β=0.379, p=0.000), while ChatGPT accuracy & responsiveness is significant for information management (β=0.212, p=0.001) and several other skills. The analysis is not an ILSA PV-based achievement prediction; it is a self-report latent-variable model, and the manuscript does not document missing-data handling or any survey-weighting strategy, limiting generalizability beyond the sampled classrooms.
